definitions.gloss: severe degree; serious level (esp. of illness or disability)
definitions.explanation: A noun used attributively (with の) to qualify illnesses, injuries, or disabilities as severe. Standard in medical and welfare contexts.

examples.japanese: {重度|じゅうど}の{障害|しょうがい}を{抱|かか}えている。
{祖父|そふ}は{重度|じゅうど}の{認知症|にんちしょう}と{診断|しんだん}された。
examples.english: My grandfather was diagnosed with severe dementia.

examples.japanese: {重度|じゅうど}の{患者|かんじゃ}には{専門|せんもん}の{医療|いりょう}スタッフが{二十四時間|にじゅうよじかん}{対応|たいおう}する。
examples.english: Specialized medical staff attend to severe-condition patients around the clock.

notes:
Compound of {重|じゅう} (heavy) + {度|ど} (degree). Used attributively in {重度|じゅうど}の + noun. Contrasts with {中度|ちゅうど} (moderate) and {軽度|けいど} (mild) to form a three-step severity scale.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {重度|じゅうど}の{障害|しょうがい}: severe disability
- {重度|じゅうど}の{認知症|にんちしょう}: severe dementia
- {重度|じゅうど}の{患者|かんじゃ}: severely ill patient
- {重度|じゅうど}の{火傷|やけど}: severe burns
- {重度|じゅうど}の{依存症|いぞんしょう}: severe addiction

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {軽度|けいど}: mild degree — antonym
- {中度|ちゅうど}: moderate degree — between the two
- {重症|じゅうしょう}: serious condition — for the patient/illness state itself, not used attributively in the same way
